autonomous_decisions.issue: Native failure `detail` is never bounded. `_failure_observations` passes the raw message straight into the `activity.message`, `session.failed` and `rate_limit.started` payloads, and `Observation` only sanitizes, it does not truncate. Confirmed: a 20000-char `turn.failed` message yields two observations with 20015-char details, and a top-level `error` keeps all 20000 chars. Frames up to 1 MiB pass through, and the rate-limit record duplicates them. The contract caps text/detail at 4096, and Claude's `failure_payload` bounds at source (src/ovcaq/drivers/claude_events.py:261). Fix: `detail = sanitize_text(detail)[:4096]` after classification, plus a regression test
autonomous_decisions.reason: Mechanical bound/sanitization fix after full-text classification, with independent regressions.

autonomous_decisions.issue: `CodexDriver.decode` raises on valid-JSON records that carry `NaN` or `Infinity` (which `json.loads` accepts) inside an MCP `result` or web `results`. `sanitize_json` raises `ValueError("JSON numbers must be finite")` out of `mcp_detail`/`web_detail`, confirmed with a one-line mcp_tool_call record. The shared `RawFirstDecoder` catch keeps the supervisor alive. But the driver's own contract ("never raise, return raw.unknown with a specific reason") fails, and the evidence reason drops to the generic "driver failed to decode frame". Deep nesting near the recursion limit takes the same path. Fix at the boundary: either `json.loads(raw_line, parse_constant=<raise ValueError>)`, which codex.py:165 already catches, or catch `(ValueError, TypeError, RecursionError)` in the two detail helpers. Add a malformed-record test
autonomous_decisions.reason: Mechanical direct-decoder totality fix for nonfinite/deep malformed detail, before state mutation.

autonomous_decisions.issue: Probe capture misses the bounded 16 KiB stdout/stderr contract. `--version` stdout streams into an unbounded `TemporaryFile`; only the 4096-byte read is capped. Auth stdout and all stderr go to DEVNULL, so an auth failure reports only "authentication check failed", with no exit code and no `codex login` hint. The contract asks for "sanitized actionable detail". This is a carried Pat MEDIUM/LOW that is still open. Capture through a pipe with a hard 16 KiB cap, and add the exit code and a login hint to the sanitized detail
autonomous_decisions.reason: Mechanical accepted 16 KiB probe-capture contract and actionable sanitized failure detail; fixture/fake checks only.

autonomous_decisions.issue: Checked-in `connectivity-failed.jsonl` fixture does not classify as connectivity. Its message "Connection failed: unable to reach example endpoint." matches none of the connectivity patterns, so the classifier returns `unknown` (confirmed by running it). The fixture test can't catch this because it builds its expected value by calling `classify_failure` itself (tests/drivers/test_codex_decode_terminals.py:120). The decision matrix skips the fixture and uses a made-up "connection refused" string instead (tests/runtime/test_codex_decisions.py:138). Phase B exit ("fixture matrix produces expected summaries") fails for this family.

autonomous_decisions.issue: Failure classifier is not based on real Codex 0.160.0 error text (checked against upstream `codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs` at tag rust-v0.160.0). These real messages all come back `unknown`: "stream disconnected before completion: …" (Codex's main network failure), "Quota exceeded. Check your plan and billing details.", "internal error; agent loop died unexpectedly", "sandbox error: …", "Selected model is at capacity". Impact: a real network drop uses the died-retry budget (default 1) and then parks or halts, instead of the connectivity wait (3 retries, 1800 s).
autonomous_decisions.reason: Additive-only HIGH: extend provider-edge diagnostic recognition with pinned upstream evidence and independent regressions; preserve precedence/unknown fallback, no public API/data-model change.

deferred_decisions.issue: The fix for R21 (interrupted/shutdown/not_found lanes) also catches lanes that already finished. The "started" set at codex.py:372 is built from every lane identity, including ones marked done. So a lane that completed and is later reported as `shutdown` (for example by a `close_agent` or `wait` call) emits `lane.failed`, and the TUI accepts the change from completed to failed. Confirmed by running it: running → completed → shutdown gives `['tool.completed', 'lane.failed']`. Fix: pass only lanes that are not done (`{lane for (cat, lane), done in self._identities.items() if cat == "lane" and not done}`), make `started_lanes` a required parameter (codex_events.py:205, its only caller always passes it), and add a test for completed-then-shutdown
deferred_decisions.reason: rework cap reached with this finding unresolved

deferred_decisions.issue: `bounded_detail` redacts credentials first and strips terminal controls second. A key split by an escape sequence therefore survives redaction and is joined back together. Confirmed: `bounded_detail("token sk-abc\x1b[0mdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ABCDEF")` returns the full `sk-abcdef…` key unredacted, and that text lands in persisted `session.failed`, `rate_limit.started` and lane payloads. The existing `_bounded` (src/ovcaq/supervisor_cli.py:77) strips first and then sanitizes. Fix: swap the order, add a regression test, and consider sharing one helper instead of a second copy of the ANSI regex

deferred_decisions.issue: The R16 activity view drops the detail on error and warning messages. `_observe_activity` reads only `payload["text"]`, but the Codex provisional top-level `error` (codex.py:278) and Claude `rate_limit_warning` (claude_events.py:143) carry their message in `detail`, so they render as a bare "error" or "rate_limit_warning". deferred_decisions.issue: A single valid Codex record can crash the supervisor, which breaks the "malformed input degrades to `raw.unknown`" rule. Any JSON string holding a lone surrogate escape (a `thread_id`, agent text, error message) passes `CodexDriver.decode` unsanitized. `NormalizedEventWriter.write` then raises `UnicodeEncodeError` at `.encode("utf-8")`. That write sits outside the decoder's `try`, so the error escapes `RawFirstDecoder.feed`. `_stream` then SIGKILLs the child, and `_attempt` re-raises. Confirmed with a one-line repro: `{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"m","type":"agent_message","text":"\ud800"}}` gives `UnicodeEncodeError: surrogates not allowed`. The state layer already rejects lone surrogates; the event path does not.
deferred_decisions.reason: rework cap reached with this finding unresolved
